faq.answer: The most common ACGME duty hour violations involve exceeding the 80-hour weekly work limit, failing to provide minimum 10-hour rest periods between shifts, and violating the 24-hour maximum continuous duty cap. Programs also frequently encounter violations when moonlighting hours are not counted toward the weekly total or when subspecialty-specific rules are inadvertently overlooked. Manual scheduling processes are especially prone to these errors because compliance is checked after a schedule is built rather than enforced during construction.
faq.question: What are the most common ACGME duty hour violations in residency programs?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard prevents ACGME duty hour violations by enforcing compliance rules mathematically at schedule generation time by a team that does this full time. Rather than producing a schedule and then checking it against duty hour rules, our team treats every ACGME regulation as a rule the schedule must satisfy before it is delivered. Subspecialty-specific rules are built into the schedule itself, so programs receive a finished, compliant schedule without any manual checking required.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard prevent ACGME duty hour violations?

faq.answer: If a duty hour violation is identified after a schedule is published, the affected portion of the schedule must be revised and redistributed, which can disrupt the entire program. Scheduling Wizard addresses this upstream by building compliance into the schedule at creation time. For mid-year changes that introduce new rules, our team can re-optimize affected portions of the schedule without requiring a full rebuild.
faq.question: What happens if a duty hour violation is found after a schedule is published?

faq.answer: Yes. Subspecialty-specific ACGME duty hour rules are built into the schedule itself. ACGME compliance is the most common question asked during onboarding, and the service is designed to handle the nuances that vary across residency and fellowship programs. Programs should communicate their specific requirements during the rule submission process so our team can apply the correct rules for their specialty.
